info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description: Public VM and control-plane API contract. Every supported deployment exposes the same wire shapes. Features that are unavailable in a selected region or provider return an `ErrorResponse` with `code: "unsupported_operation"`.

Replaces the complete network policy of a mutable VM owned by the authenticated caller and applies it to the running VM. Rules in the ordered list get ids `rule-0`, `rule-1`, ... and priorities that keep their order. Public base VMs are immutable.

The run finished inside the synchronous window. `state` is terminal and `exit_code` is the command's real status.

202.description: Accepted - the run is still executing. The body carries `run_id` and `state: "running"`, not output; poll `GET /v1/vms/{id}/runs/{run_id}` for the result. Returned for `time_to_background: 0` and whenever the command outstays `time_to_background`. A 2xx here means the request was accepted, not that the work is done.

post.description: Run a command. Set `time_to_background` to `0` to return a pollable run immediately after successful dispatch. A positive value bounds the synchronous wait, and omission uses the default window. A run that is still executing when the response is sent returns **202 Accepted** with a `run_id`; only a run that finished returns 200. Control requests do not accept `time_to_background`. `timeout` is the separate execution and kill bound. The request body is limited to 4 MiB (4194304 bytes) and a larger one returns 413. Write files with `sync` instead of embedding their content in `command`.

patch.summary: Update a session (resize PTY / set timeout)
patch.description: Resize the session's PTY (cols/rows) and/or update its idle timeout. A resize applies at once to the session's open terminal, attached or detached, and is the size the next attach opens at. REST equivalent of the WebSocket {"type":"resize"} control frame - usable from any client, attached or not.

delete.description: Close and remove a persistent VM session. Every run admitted to the session ends `cancelled`, including queued and backgrounded runs, and everything the session started, detached processes included, is stopped. A request that names the session after the delete begins is refused. If the delete cannot complete it returns 503, and the session stays hidden and refuses new runs until a retried delete finishes it.

parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Initial terminal width in columns.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Initial terminal height in rows.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Single executable path to launch (no shell-splitting). Defaults to the login shell.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: When true (default), disconnecting keeps the shell running so the same session_id can reconnect to it and receive recent scrollback. When false, the shell is terminated on disconnect. A kill control message or the configured idle TTL terminates a persistent shell.

parameters.name: cancel_ttl_secs
parameters.description: Destroy the PTY after this many seconds without terminal input or output. Omit or set to zero to disable this PTY-specific idle limit.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Browser auth: a short-lived ticket from POST .../pty-ticket, used in place of the Authorization header (which a browser WebSocket cannot set).

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying an interactive pseudo-terminal in the VM, reusing the same interactive terminal as SSH. Authenticate with a bearer API key or, for browser clients, a short-lived PTY ticket. Reopening the same `session_id` reconnects to a persistent shell and replays recent scrollback. Binary server frames contain raw terminal output; binary client frames contain stdin bytes. Text client frames accept JSON controls for `resize`, `kill`, and `ping`. Closing the socket detaches a persistent shell or destroys a non-persistent shell; `kill` always destroys it. The service enforces attachment limits and closes oversized or idle connections.

101.description: Switching Protocols - the WebSocket PTY stream is established.

post.description: Returns a short-lived, multi-use credential for opening the PTY WebSocket from a browser, which cannot set an Authorization header. The bearer-authenticated caller must own the VM. Pass the returned credential as the `ticket` query parameter on the PTY WebSocket URL.

Mount an existing filesystem into this VM at `path`. Repeating the same filesystem and path returns the existing mount. Returns `ErrorResponse` code `conflict` if another filesystem occupies the path or this filesystem is mounted at another path on the VM.

parameters.name: filesystem_id
parameters.description: Return only mounts for this filesystem.

delete.description: Remove a persistent filesystem mount from a VM.

200.description: Read or write result, matching the request op.

post.description:
Read or write files in the VM filesystem. Op-discriminated:
`{op:"read",path}` reads a file (inline content for small files, a
presigned GET URL for large ones); `{op:"write",writes:[...]}` writes,
each entry an inline chunk or a presigned-upload step. Binding a
filesystem into the VM is the separate `/v1/vms/{id}/mounts` resource.

get.description: List the organization's pools in this region, newest first; at https://arker.ai/api without a `region` query parameter, in every region. A key limited to a pool lists that pool only. A pool being deleted is listed until it is gone. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum pools per page.

post.description: Create a pool accessible through the regional endpoint used to invoke this operation. A `managed` pool starts `running`; a `byoc` or `self_hosted` pool starts `creating`. Requires an admin API key not limited to a VM or pool. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization. `self_hosted` pools may be unavailable, and creating one then returns 422 `unsupported_operation`. Returns 429 `quota_exceeded` when the organization already has as many pools in the region as its `pools` quota allows, or when a `managed` pool would take the organization's `managed` pools in the region past its `vcpus`, `ram_mib` or `disk_mib` quota.

get.description: Return one of the organization's pools, including while it is `deleting`. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization.

patch.description: Rename or resize a pool; commitments may be unavailable. Requires an admin API key with access to the pool. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization. Growing a `managed` pool returns 429 `quota_exceeded` when the organization's `managed` pools in the region would reserve more than its `vcpus`, `ram_mib` or `disk_mib` quota.

delete.description: Do NOT invoke this unless you're sure you want to completely delete the pool. Resize to zero in most cases, e.g. to end Arker billing. The pool turns `deleting`, its workers are told to leave, every VM in it is deleted, and its API keys are revoked once it is gone. Refused during a commitment. Deleting a pool that is already deleting answers the same way. Requires an admin API key with access to the pool. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization.

get.description: List the workers of a `byoc` or `self_hosted` pool. Unsupported on a `managed` pool. Returns 404 when pools are not enabled for the organization.

put.description: Join the pool, or keep the worker in it. The first worker of a `self_hosted` pool sets its platform; the heartbeat's `platform` must be the pool's and its `kind` one the pool takes; a retired worker id is refused. Authenticate with an API key limited to this pool. A worker id the pool has not seen gets 429 `quota_exceeded` while the pool has as many workers as its `pool_workers` quota allows; it joins once another leaves.

200.description: The worker is in the pool.

get.description: Opens the authenticated worker tunnel. Requires the worker to have joined. Authenticate with an API key limited to this pool.

put.description: Record the VM as it is now; send it again on every change. Arker lists the VM from this record. Only a VM Arker forked onto this worker; any other VM is not found. Authenticate with an API key limited to this pool.

delete.description: Record that the VM is gone. Only a VM Arker forked onto this worker; any other VM is not found. Authenticate with an API key limited to this pool.

204.description: The VM is recorded as deleted.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run identifier the worker chose.

put.description: Record a run when it starts and again when it ends. Arker answers `listRuns` and `getRun` for the VM from these records. Only a VM Arker forked onto this worker; any other VM is not found. Authenticate with an API key limited to this pool.

get.description: List the organization's unrevoked API keys, newest first. A key limited to a pool manages that pool's keys only; a key limited to VMs manages none.

post.description: Create an API key, optionally limited to VMs or one pool. The key has its creator's role and is returned only once. A key limited to a pool manages that pool's keys only; a key limited to VMs manages none.

delete.description: Revoke an API key; requests with it are refused from then on. A key limited to a pool manages that pool's keys only; a key limited to VMs manages none.

PtyTicket.description: Short-lived browser credential created by the PTY ticket endpoint.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes the request safely retryable. Reusing a key with the same request returns the original result - the same run, or the same VM for a fork - instead of doing the work twice; reusing it with a different request returns a conflict. A fork whose key is claimed but still running answers 503 with a retry hint, since the VM it would name does not exist yet.

VmId.name: id
VmId.description: VM identifier: a VM id, or a name. Names resolve in the public base-VM registry first (e.g. ubuntu-full), then among the calling organization's own named VMs. Names never have the shape of a VM id.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum items per page. Service caps may apply.

RetryAfter.description: Delay in seconds before retrying a transiently unavailable request.

Allow.description: Required on 405. Comma-separated allowed HTTP methods, matching error.details.allowed_methods.

WwwAuthenticate.description: Required authentication challenge for a 401 response. Do not include credentials or internal authentication failure details.

Error.description: Public error envelope. This full-catalog fallback does not define the permitted errors for an individual endpoint; explicit response sets narrow the union.

BadRequestError.description: HTTP 400: The request is malformed or its fields fail validation. Correct the request using the message and optional field violations.

error.message: The uploaded file does not match its expected checksum.

violations.message: The digest must match the uploaded content.

bad_request.description: The file operation stopped after checksum rejection. The VM may remain running; prior VM start, directory creation or staging writes are not promised to be rolled back.

InsufficientResourcesError.description: HTTP 400: The requested allocation is too small for the operation. Increase the specified allocation. This does not mean the fleet lacks capacity.

error.message: The image does not fit the requested disk allocation.

UnauthorizedError.description: HTTP 401: Valid authentication is missing or invalid. Supply or refresh credentials.

error.message: Valid authentication credentials are required.

ForbiddenError.description: HTTP 403: The caller or policy does not permit this operation. Obtain access or change the applicable policy; repeating the same request does not resolve it.

error.message: You do not have permission to perform this operation.

NotFoundError.description: HTTP 404: The requested resource or route is not available to this caller. Check the identifier and scope; do not assume this distinguishes missing from inaccessible.

error.message: The requested VM was not found.

ConflictError.description: HTTP 409: The request conflicts with current state, with no more specific handling below. Read the current state and update the request. This is the fallback for known state conflicts.

error.message: The request conflicts with the current session state.

ResourceBusyError.description: HTTP 409: Active work temporarily prevents the requested operation. Wait for or finish the conflicting work, then retry when the operation is safe to repeat.

error.message: This session is already attached.

InvalidStateError.description: HTTP 409: The operation requires a different resource state. Perform the prerequisite or choose another resource. An inbound policy refusing to start the VM uses running; a start already in progress uses unavailable.

error.message: This operation requires a mutable VM. Select or fork a mutable VM.

AlreadyExistsError.description: HTTP 409: A resource or unique name already exists. Use the existing resource or choose another name.

error.message: A VM with the requested destination name already exists.

IdempotencyConflictError.description: HTTP 409: An idempotency key is bound to a different request. Reuse the original request or intentionally use a new key.

error.message: This idempotency key was already used for a different request.

ExpiredError.description: HTTP 410: A time-limited resource is known to have expired. Create a replacement. Use not_found when missing and expired cannot be distinguished.

error.message: The SSH setup resource has expired. Create a replacement.

PayloadTooLargeError.description: HTTP 413: A request or transfer exceeds the supported byte limit. Reduce or split the payload. This is different from insufficient VM disk allocation.

error.message: The request body exceeds the supported byte limit.

MethodNotAllowedError.description: HTTP 405: The route does not support this HTTP method. Use an allowed method.

error.message: This HTTP method is not allowed for this route.

UnsupportedOperationError.description: HTTP 422: The selected runtime, platform or feature cannot serve the requested operation. Select a supported operation or platform. For restore_requires_birth_host, restore through an eligible host; do not recreate solely because this host cannot restore it.

error.message: The selected platform does not support shared filesystems.

UnrecoverableError.description: HTTP 422: Authoritative state establishes that recoverable resource state is lost. Recreate only after loss is established. Missing local files, an unknown owner or a host-specific restore restriction are insufficient evidence.

error.message: Authoritative state confirms that recoverable VM state has been lost.

CapacityUnavailableError.description: HTTP 503: The platform currently lacks capacity to admit otherwise valid work. Wait, release capacity, or select another placement. The requested allocation itself can be valid.

error.message: The worker cannot currently admit the requested allocation.

UnavailableError.description: HTTP 503: A required service or operation is temporarily unavailable. Retry only when the operation is safe to repeat; the code does not guarantee absence of side effects.

error.message: The VM recovery state is temporarily unavailable.

InternalError.description: HTTP 500: An unexpected implementation failure prevents completion. Use a safe message and correlation identifier for support; log the internal cause.

error.message: An internal error prevented image configuration from completing.

RateLimitedError.description: HTTP 429: A request-rate limiter rejects the operation. For Arker limits, reduce request rate; for upstream limits, address that service’s quota or credentials.

error.message: The request rate limit was exceeded.

QuotaExceededError.description: HTTP 429: A scoped budget, resource or PTY-session limit rejects the operation. Use the exact metric, scope and measurements to release usage or adjust the applicable limit. Organization PTY counts are currently worker-local.

error.message: The VM has reached its PTY session limit.

PaymentRequiredError.description: HTTP 402: Billing setup or payment recovery is required for compute. Complete billing setup or resolve payment.

error.message: Complete billing setup or resolve payment before starting compute.

ActionRequiredError.description: HTTP 403: A specific account action must occur before this operation. Complete the named action, such as accepting legal terms or converting the billing plan.

error.message: Accept the current legal documents before continuing.

OperationFailedError.description: HTTP 422: A caller-selected image or build operation reports an expected domain failure, including an explicit execution-budget limit. Inspect the typed reason and any partial-work handles. Poll continuing work or clean up the retained VM before starting another attempt.

error.message: The build exceeded its execution budget.

GatewayTimeoutError.description: HTTP 504: A gateway or proxy did not receive a required upstream response before its deadline. Inspect known operation handles before retrying. An upstream timeout does not prove that upstream work stopped. An explicit application execution budget uses operation_failed/deadline_exceeded, not this code.

error.message: The gateway did not receive an upstream response before its deadline.

error.message: The health request could not be completed.

ErrorCode.description: Stable public error codes. ErrorBody selects the required details for each code; clients must not parse message text.

ErrorBody.description: Typed HTTP error body. The code selects its required details. Endpoint responses must narrow this union to their permitted codes.

ErrorResponse.description: Public HTTP error envelope. Every code has one HTTP status, documented on its body schema. Code/status matching is enforced at the response boundary.

VmState.description: `running` while something uses the VM: a run, an SSH connection, a terminal, an inbound request, a sync or a resize. `idle` otherwise. A Windows VM is `running` from its start until it is suspended.

SessionState.description: `running`: a run is executing or a terminal is attached. `pending`: runs are waiting for the VM to start. `idle`: neither.

RunState.description: Lifecycle state for a run. `pending` means the run was accepted but is not running: it has not started yet because an earlier run on the same session is still in flight, or its VM is suspended and it continues when the VM starts. It is not terminal, and a client should keep polling. `running` means the command is in progress. `completed` means the command finished; `exit_code` reports its result. `failed` means the service could not start or finish the command, with a client-safe explanation in `fail_reason`. `cancelled` means the client cancelled the run.

Provider.description: Infrastructure provider currently hosting the resource.

PolicyWriteRequest.description: A complete replacement for a VM's network policy. Rules are evaluated in order, and the first matching rule determines the result. An empty rule list allows all outbound traffic and permits authenticated inbound access to any guest port.

policies.description: Ordered network policy rules. An empty list allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. With an outbound `allow` rule, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. Until an inbound rule applies to requests through a port, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; after that, only the ports that inbound rules other than `deny` name are reachable.

secrets.description: Named secret values referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions, match values and `auth.token`. Values are encrypted at rest and masked in subsequent policy responses.

hostname.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read. Nullable base `.app` hostname for inbound services. The bare hostname selects guest port 8080. For another port, insert `-<port>` before the first dot: `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`. Clients must not require this field to be present.

mitm_domains.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read.

warnings.description: Server-derived; accepted and ignored on write so a client can PUT back a document it read.

PolicyDoc.description: A VM's current network policy and its derived inbound exposure metadata.

policies.description: Ordered network policy rules. An empty list allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. With an outbound `allow` rule, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. Until an inbound rule applies to requests through a port, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; after that, only the ports that inbound rules other than `deny` name are reachable.

secrets.description: Named secrets referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions, match values and `auth.token`. Stored values are represented as `***`; supply the original value when replacing a policy that uses it.

hostname.description: Nullable base `.app` hostname for inbound services. The bare hostname selects guest port 8080. For another port, insert `-<port>` before the first dot: `<vm>-<port>.<provider>-<region>.arker.app`. Clients must not require this field to be present.

mitm_domains.description: Domains whose matching traffic is evaluated by the request-level policy engine.

PolicyEntry.description: One policy rule. `match` AND's its present fields (absent ⇒ catch-all).

type.description: Traffic direction: `outbound` controls connections initiated by the VM; `inbound` exposes a guest port. Unknown values are rejected.

auth.description: Authentication for an inbound rule that exposes a port - `allow`, or a `suspend` or `scaling`-only action. `open` exposes the port publicly; `arker` requires `Authorization: Bearer $ARKER_API_KEY` from the VM owner's organization before forwarding to the guest. The default is `arker`. This field is invalid on deny and outbound rules. Inbound port matches must use individual ports rather than ranges.

PolicyMatch.description: Match criteria: present fields are combined with AND; list items are combined with OR. `ips` and `hosts` are mutually exclusive, and inbound rules cannot use `hosts`. Port, IP, and host rules operate at the connection layer. Method, path, header, query parameter, and body rules operate at the request layer.

ports.description: Single ports and/or inclusive [start, end] ranges, e.g. [80, 443, [1000, 2000]]. Absent = any port; an empty list is refused. Inbound rules other than `deny` require one or more individual ports, and inbound rules reject ranges.

ips.description: IPs or CIDRs. Outbound rules match destination IPs; inbound rules match the caller source IP.

hosts.description: Label-boundary suffix match on the request host: `github.com` matches `api.github.com`, not `evilgithub.com`.

methods.description: HTTP methods matched by this rule.

headers.description: Header name → any-of values (names AND'd, a name's values OR'd). A value may use `${secret:NAME}`. On an inbound rule, `"authorization": ["Bearer $arker_api_key"]` or `"x-api-key": ["$arker_api_key"]` matches an API key of the VM's organization.

query_params.description: Query parameter name → any-of values (names AND'd, a name's values OR'd). A value may use `${secret:NAME}`. On an inbound rule, parameters named `arker_*` are removed from a `GET` request's URL by a redirect that keeps them in a cookie, so the rest of a browsing session carries them without the URL showing them.

body_contains.description: Substrings that must appear in the request body.

vm_state.description: `inbound` only. The VM's state (`VmState`) when the request arrives: `idle` or `running`. A request a `deny` rule refuses because of `vm_state` receives `409 invalid_state` (requirement `running`); other refused requests receive `403`.

via.description: `inbound` only. How the request reaches the VM: `port` to a guest port at its `.arker.app` hostname, `ssh` over SSH, `pty` by attaching a terminal (`GET /v1/vms/{id}/sessions/{sid}/pty`). Defaults to `["port"]`. A way no rule names works as it does without rules; once a rule names it, the rules decide, and a request no rule matches is refused. A rule naming `ssh` or `pty` matches only on `ips`, `vm_state`, `connection_state` and, for `ssh` alone, `ssh_keys`, and is `allow` or `deny`. A region that does not yet pass an SSH caller's address on refuses `ips` on a rule naming `ssh`.

ssh_keys.description: `inbound` only, on a rule whose `via` is `["ssh"]`. SSH public keys in `authorized_keys` format (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment`). The rule matches an SSH login with one of these keys, compared by key, not by comment. An `allow` lets the key log in; a `deny` refuses it. Without `ssh_keys`, a `deny` naming `ssh` matches every key, and an `allow` the keys the VM knows: its own unexpired `ssh_public_keys` and the keys any `allow` lists. Once a rule names `ssh`, organization SSH keys no longer log in to the VM. A `deny` of the key that also lists `open` in `connection_state` closes its open SSH connections. Certificates, `authorized_keys` options such as `from=` or `command=`, and `ssh-dss` keys are refused. The rule opens no port.

connection_state.description: `inbound` only. The requests the rule applies to: `new` ones as they arrive, and `open` ones already in progress on the VM, such as a WebSocket, a response still streaming, an SSH connection or an attached terminal, matched on the request that opened them. A request in progress meets only the rules listing `open`, by priority, each time the VM's policies are written: an `allow` keeps it, a `deny` closes it, and one no such rule matches stays open. Only an `allow` or a `deny` may list `open`. An idle keep-alive connection holds nothing, so its next request is `new`. Defaults to `["new"]`.

oneOf.description: The object action: at least one of `rewrite` / `gate` / `suspend` must be present. The request is forwarded upstream (applying `rewrite` if present); a `gate` blocks it until an outbound HTTP check allows it; `suspend` suspends the VM until its response arrives. The three compose freely on one action.

suspend.description: `outbound` only. `true` does what the `suspend` action does, alongside `rewrite` or `gate`: allows the request and suspends the VM until its response arrives.

PolicyAction.description: allow / deny, `delete` (schedule rules), `suspend` (schedule and outbound rules: suspends the VM; on outbound, allows the request and suspends the VM until its response arrives), or an object with any combination of `rewrite`, `gate`, and `suspend` (at least one).

ScaleAction.description: Scales the VM when the rule matches or fires. On an `outbound` rule `suspend` brackets the time the VM is blocked awaiting an upstream response; on an `inbound` rule it suspends the VM once a matched request has been answered. Outbound rules may be narrowed by request fields (`methods`/`paths`/`headers`/`body_contains`), for example to suspend only on `POST /v1/messages`, and compose with `rewrite` / `gate` siblings. For outbound, prefer a `match.hosts` scope: a host-less rule matches every flow it can see, which breaks certificate-pinning clients.

suspend.description: Suspend the VM (snapshot and free CPU/RAM). On an `outbound` rule: while a matched upstream request is blocked, resuming when the response arrives. On an `inbound` rule (deprecated): once a matched request's response has been fully delivered and nothing else is in flight, so the next matched request starts it again. On an `outbound` rule, matched responses are delivered only once the upstream response is COMPLETE: a suspended VM has no running guest to receive bytes, so the proxy holds the whole body and hands it over at the end. Total latency is unchanged, but a response whose fragments are individually usable - an SSE token stream, for example - stops arriving incrementally, so a client rendering tokens as they arrive will see nothing until the response finishes. Enabling this is a deliberate trade of incremental delivery for the memory saving.

wake.description: Deprecated: put a rule matching `vm_state: "idle"` with action `deny` ahead of this one instead. Whether a matched inbound request may start an idle VM; absent allows it. `false` answers a request received while the VM is `idle` with `409 invalid_state` (requirement `running`); requests received while the VM is running are served normally. Not valid on outbound rules.

Rewrite.description: Mutate-and-forward. Host/path/header/body values support request-time `$`-token interpolation: `$domain`, `$path`, `$method`, `$vm_id`, `$body` (the request body as received, also `${…}`-braced), `${header:NAME}` (the request's header NAME, on inbound rules), and `$$` for a literal `$`. Unknown/unresolved tokens pass through unchanged.

remove_headers.description: Request header names to remove before forwarding.

remove_query_params.description: Query parameter names to remove from the URL before forwarding.

body.description: Replace the request body entirely with this (interpolated) value; `$body` re-injects the original body. Absent = body forwarded unchanged.

Gate.description: `action.gate` performs an outbound HTTP authorization check before opening the VM's matching connection. A response status in `allow_on_status` permits the connection and applies any sibling `rewrite`; any other status denies it. Timeouts and connection failures follow `deny_on_timeout`, which defaults to deny. `path`, header values, and string leaves of `body` support `$` substitution with the documented request variables. `host` is not substituted. Injected JSON values are escaped, and gate requests reject private, link-local, and internal destinations.

headers.description: Request headers with interpolated values. Stored credentials are encrypted at rest and masked in policy responses.

allow_on_status.description: HTTP status codes that mean ALLOW. Any other status denies. Must be non-empty.

deny_on_timeout.description: Verdict on timeout / connection failure: true = deny (fail-closed, default), false = allow (fail-open).

Create a session with `POST /v1/vms/{id}/sessions`, which also sets its starting directory and environment, then pass its id here. Run sequential commands in one session; for a long-running task, use `time_to_background: 0` in a session of its own so later work does not interrupt it. Distinct sessions run concurrently. A run completes when its command exits; processes it leaves running in the background are not waited on, and this timeout does not apply to them once the run has completed. If it fires before the command exits, the command and every process it started are killed, including background ones.

gpu_sms.description: Number of GPU streaming multiprocessors available to the VM on EACH of its GPUs (a per-GPU value, uniform across the VM's devices; see `gpu_count`). Reported on GPU platforms such as `x86_64-l40s`. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`. `0` means the VM was forked with `vgpu: 0` and holds no GPU; an absent field means the VM has no GPU at all.

gpu_vram_mib.description: GPU memory available to the VM, in MiB, on EACH of its GPUs (a per-GPU value; see `gpu_count`). Reported on GPU platforms. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`. `0` means the VM was forked with `vgpu: 0` and holds no GPU; an absent field means the VM has no GPU at all.

gpu_count.description: Number of physical GPUs attached to the VM. `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` are per-GPU values applied uniformly to every attached device, so the VM's total GPU allocation (and quota charge) is `gpu_count x per-GPU`. Reported on GPU platforms. Response-only: a fork sizes GPU with `vgpu`, and this is the card count that implies. `0` means the VM was forked with `vgpu: 0` and holds no GPU; an absent field means the VM has no GPU at all.

VmResources.description: Resources a VM actually holds. GPU values are per-GPU; see `gpu_count` for the VM's total.

Vgpu.description: How much GPU, measured in cards. Below one card: eighths of ONE card. At or above one: whole cards, and the VM holds that many devices - `gpu_sms` and `gpu_vram_mib` are per-GPU, so its total is `gpu_count` times those. 0 declines a GPU and yields a CPU-only VM. The enum is the ladder: there is no 1.5 of a card, and no 3-card worker to be given.

vgpu.description: Fraction of one physical GPU to allocate, in eighths of a card: 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625, 0.75, 0.875, or 1. Resolved against the serving platform's GPU (`vgpu: 0.25` on `x86_64-l40s` is 35 SMs and 11517 MiB), so the same fraction is a different amount of silicon on a different card - see the per-platform table in the docs. Mutually exclusive with `gpu_sms` and `gpu_vram_mib`. Request-only: responses report the resolved `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` and never this field.

ResourcesInput.description: Resource shape a caller asks for. GPU size is set with `vgpu`, in eighths of one card; the resolved per-GPU `gpu_sms`/`gpu_vram_mib` are reported back on the machine.

immutable.description: Make the VM immutable. Only `true` is accepted, and it must be the only field in its request: an immutable VM cannot be made mutable again. An immutable VM can be viewed, listed, forked, and deleted, and every request that would change it or start it is refused. A running VM is refused with `resource_busy`; retry once it is idle. Repeating the request for an immutable VM changes nothing.

CPU, memory, and disk limits come from the source VM; GPU limits come from the platform catalog.

PolicyRule.description: One network policy rule, keyed by its id in a policy's `rules`. `match` ANDs its present fields (absent ⇒ catch-all). Rules are evaluated highest `priority` first, and the first rule that matches decides.

type.description: Traffic direction: `outbound` controls connections initiated by the VM; `inbound` exposes a guest port. Unknown values are rejected.

priority.description: Evaluation rank from 0 to 1000000: higher priorities are evaluated first. No two rules of a policy may share a priority. Leave gaps between priorities so a rule can later be ranked between two others.

auth.description: Deprecated: put the credential a request must carry in `match`. For inbound `allow` rules. `arker` requires an API key for the VM's organization, `open` requires none, and `{"token": ...}` accepts the token in the `arker_token` query parameter or cookie, or an API key. Omitted, the rule's `match` alone decides.

expires_at.description: Inbound rules only. An RFC 3339 time in the future. After it, the rule no longer applies.

PolicyUpdate.description: A change to a VM's network policy: only the rules and secrets named are written or removed, and everything else is kept, so `{}` changes nothing. The deprecated `policies` list instead replaces the whole policy.

rules.description: Rules to write, keyed by rule id. A rule replaces any rule with the same id; `null` removes the rule with that id. Rules not named here are kept. The resulting policy must not give two rules of one `type` the same priority.

secrets.description: Secrets to write, referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions, match values and `auth.token`. A value replaces the secret with that name; `null` removes it. Secrets not named here are kept. Values are encrypted at rest and masked as `***` in responses; `***` is not accepted as a value.

policies.description: Deprecated: an ordered rule list that replaces the whole policy, first match wins. An empty list clears it. Use `rules`. Cannot be combined with `rules`.

VmPolicies.description: The VM's network policy. Change it with `policies` on `PATCH /v1/vms/{id}`.

rules.description: The VM's network policy rules, keyed by rule id (1-64 characters: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; starting with a letter or digit). Rules are evaluated highest `priority` first, and the first matching rule decides. No rules allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. With an outbound `allow` rule, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. Until an inbound rule applies to requests through a port, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; after that, only the ports that inbound rules other than `deny` name are reachable.

secrets.description: Names of the secrets referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in rewrite actions, match values and `auth.token`. Values are masked as `***`.

mitm_domains.description: Domains whose matching traffic is evaluated by the request-level policy engine.

PolicyRules.description: The VM's network policy rules, keyed by rule id (1-64 characters: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; starting with a letter or digit). Rules are evaluated highest `priority` first, and the first matching rule decides. No rules allows all outbound traffic and permits inbound traffic to any guest port after Arker authentication. With an outbound `allow` rule, unmatched outbound traffic is denied. Until an inbound rule applies to requests through a port, inbound access keeps the authenticated default; after that, only the ports that inbound rules other than `deny` name are reachable.

public_key.description: SSH public key in `authorized_keys` format, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@host`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp from which the key no longer authorizes logins; must be in the future when written. Omit it for a key that never expires.

SshKeysUpdate.description: SSH keys to write, keyed by key id (1-64 characters: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; starting with a letter or digit). A key replaces any key with the same id; `null` removes the key with that id. Keys not named here are kept, so `{}` changes nothing. The resulting set must not hold one public key under two ids.

ScheduleRule.description: A rule that acts on the VM itself when its clock fires. It names exactly one clock: `at` a time, `after_created`, or `after_last_running_start`. It has no `priority` and does not affect traffic.

at.description: When the rule fires: an RFC 3339 time. On a `suspend` rule, a time that has already come fires it at once; on a `delete` rule, the time must be in the future.

after_created.description: Fires this many seconds, up to 2592000 (30 days), after the VM was created; a fork counts from its own creation.

after_last_running_start.description: Fires this many seconds, up to 2592000 (30 days), after the VM last became `running`, and again each time it starts running; a VM that never ran counts from its creation.

action.description: `delete` deletes the VM, as `DELETE /v1/vms/{id}` does, also while it is suspended. `suspend` suspends the VM once, if it is running when the rule fires, ending every use of it: its connections close, its terminals detach and its runs go `pending` until something next starts it, which the other rules still allow. A sync or resize in progress finishes first. A VM that is idle then is left alone.

LifecycleRule.description: Deprecated: use a `schedule` rule. Deletes the VM at a set time, or a set number of seconds after it was created.

at.description: An RFC 3339 time in the future.

after.description: Seconds after the VM's creation, up to 2592000 (30 days).

name.description: Pool name, unique and case-insensitive within the pool's region.

isolation.description: What the pool keeps in your cloud account instead of Arker's regional store. Defaults to `["vms"]`.

name.description: Pool name, unique and case-insensitive within the pool's region.

resources.description: Resources requested: a cap on `resources_reserved`. Absent means no cap.

CreatePoolRequest.description: A regional pool. Run on multi-cloud managed compute, BYOC in an arbitrary cloud account, or self-hosted using BLAST. If BYOC or self-hosted, a significant discount is applied against on-demand rates and organization limits are not applied.

name.description: New pool name, or null to remove it.

resources.description: New requested resources. Growing is always allowed; shrinking, including to zero, only while no commitment is active.

commitments.description: Commitments may be unavailable, and a request that then sets one is refused with 422 unsupported_operation; `[]` is always accepted. The full list of commitments; one that has started must be kept unchanged. Managed pools only.

WorkerKind.description: The software the worker runs. A `self_hosted` pool takes `blast` workers only, and a `byoc` pool takes `arkerd` workers only.

WorkerHeartbeatState.description: `bootstrapping` is still starting and takes no VMs yet; `active` takes new VMs; `draining` keeps its VMs but takes no new ones; `left` has handed back its VMs and left the pool for good, and its id cannot rejoin. A worker that stops without leaving keeps its id and rejoins as `active`.

WorkerState.description: `creating` is starting and takes no VMs yet; `running` takes new VMs; `draining` keeps its VMs but takes no new ones; `unreachable` has missed its heartbeats or lost its tunnel, and its VMs answer `unavailable` until it returns; `left` has left the pool for good.

resources_provisioned.description: What the worker's VMs use right now; nothing unless the worker is `running` or `draining`.

resources_reserved.description: What the worker adds to the pool's `resources_reserved`; nothing unless it is `running` or `draining`.

WorkerHeartbeat.description: A worker joins the pool in the path with its first heartbeat and stays in it until it reports `left`; a stopped worker rejoins under the same id. Fields Arker does not know are ignored, so a newer worker heartbeats to an older Arker.

platform.description: The platform the worker serves; a BLAST worker's `blast-<arch>` is `smolvm-<arch>`. The first worker of a `self_hosted` pool sets the pool's platform; every other must match it.

golden_env.description: Runtime configuration reported by a `byoc` worker.

goldens.description: Images the worker cannot currently serve. Absent when all configured images are available.

vm_activity.description: For a `byoc` pool's arkerd worker: its VMs forked often enough to prewarm on the pool's other workers, by VM id. Arker ignores a VM that is not in the worker's pool.

cached_record_ids.description: For a `byoc` pool's arkerd worker: the records it holds, so Arker does not ask it to prewarm one again.

WorkerVmActivity.description: One VM's recent activity on the worker that reports it.

forks.description: Forks of the VM within the activity window.

WorkerGoldens.description: Images a worker cannot currently serve, by name.

stale.description: Images for which the worker has an outdated version.

missing.description: Images unavailable on this worker. A fork from one of these images fails.

WorkerStorageCredentials.description: Short-lived AWS credentials for `prefix` of `bucket`; every heartbeat answer carries ones that are still fresh.

prefix.description: Key prefix the credentials may read and write under; empty for the whole bucket.

WorkerHeartbeatResponse.description: A worker ignores fields it does not know, so an older worker heartbeats to a newer Arker.

worker_id.description: The worker identifier from the path.

heartbeat_interval_ms.description: Send the next heartbeat after this long.

desired_state.description: The state Arker wants the worker in. `left` once the pool is deleting.

tunnel_url.description: WebSocket URL the worker keeps open so Arker can reach it; a path is relative to the endpoint the heartbeat went to.

upgrade_release_id.description: Target release while a worker upgrade is pending.

golden_env.description: Desired runtime configuration for a `byoc` worker.

WorkerVmRecord.description: A VM a BLAST worker holds, as it reports it. The VM runs the pool's platform.

state.description: `running` executes; `paused` keeps its memory but no CPU; `suspended` is a snapshot in storage.

image.description: Image the VM was created from, if any.

parent_vm_id.description: VM this one was forked from, if any: a VM in the same pool.

last_active_at.description: When the VM last ran a command or was synced.

WorkerRunRecord.description: A run on a BLAST worker's VM, as the worker reports it when the run starts and again when it ends.

state.description: `running` until the command ends; then `completed` (it exited), `failed` (the worker could not run or finish it) or `cancelled`.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status once it has one.

finished_at.description: When the run ended; null while it runs.

ApiKeyScope.description: A VM or a pool an API key is limited to.

ApiKeyVmScope.description: A VM the key acts on.

ApiKeyPoolScope.description: The pool the key acts on.

pool_id.description: The pool. The key manages the pool, forks into it by default, and lists only its VMs and runs; the workers of a `self_hosted` pool call with it.

ApiKey.description: An API key. It acts with the role of the user or key that created it, limited by `scopes`.

api_key_id.description: API key identifier; starts with the `name` given at creation.

role.description: Deprecated: the role the key acts with, its creator's: `admin` or `member`.

scopes.description: What the key is limited to: VMs, or one pool.

vm_id.description: Deprecated: read `scopes`. The VM when the key is limited to exactly one, else null.

pool_id.description: Deprecated: read `scopes`. The pool the key is limited to, or null.

CreatedApiKey.description: A new API key and its secret.

api_key_id.description: API key identifier; starts with the `name` given at creation.

role.description: Deprecated: the role the key acts with, its creator's: `admin` or `member`.

scopes.description: What the key is limited to: VMs, or one pool.

vm_id.description: Deprecated: read `scopes`. The VM when the key is limited to exactly one, else null.

pool_id.description: Deprecated: read `scopes`. The pool the key is limited to, or null.

key.description: The key. Shown only in this response.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: A new key has its creator's role.

name.description: A label that starts `api_key_id`: lowercased, other characters than `a-z0-9_-` as `-`, cut to 13 characters.

scopes.description: What the key is limited to: 1 to 16 VMs of the organization, or one of its pools. Only admins create a key limited to a pool.

EventAction.description: What an event records. `run` includes a PTY attach; `delete` a VM's deletion; `inbound_request` a request to one of the VM's ports; `outbound_request` a request the VM's network policy refused; `ssh_session` one SSH connection; `sign_in` a member's session entering the organization, by signing in or switching to it.

id.description: The action's id, the same while it is running and once it ends.

vm_id.description: The VM the action used; a fork's new VM. Null for an action on no VM.

requested_at.description: When the request arrived, or an automatic action was triggered.

started_at.description: When the action began executing; null before it does and for an action with no separate start.

ended_at.description: When the action ended; null while it is running.

duration_ms.description: From `started_at`, or `requested_at` when there is none, to `ended_at`; null while running.

actor.description: Who initiated the action, and how. Null for an automatic action, or when Arker does not know who acted.

region.description: The region that served the action; null for one the console served, such as an API key's.

request_id.description: The `x-request-id` of the request that made the action.

error_code.description: Why the action failed or was refused.

attributes.description: Facts only some actions have, such as a run's `run_id` and `exit_code`, a fork's `source_vm_id`, or an inbound request's `port`.

id.description: Who: a member's email in the console; an API key's `api_key_id`; an SSH key's id, or its fingerprint when it is no account key. None when Arker acted.

EventVia.description: How an action was initiated: by a member in the console, with an API key, over SSH with an SSH key, or by Arker.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when there is none.
